messages:
maya: bringing up HF repo https://huggingface.co/org/raptor-xl on Redwood. conversion step errors out because model uses a custom class (not in transformers core). also seeing tokenizer special tokens disappear after our quantization pass — evals drop ~3-4 pts. any quick ideas?

liam: can you paste the conversion log + repo link?

maya: repo above + log excerpt: 
```
ERROR: auto_map failed to resolve class RaptorForCausalLM_v2 -> ImportError: cannot import name 'RaptorForCausalLM_v2' from 'raptor.model'
During conversion: tokenizer.special_tokens_map missing '<|system|>'
```

oliver: yep this is a trust_remote_code situation. HF model defines a custom architecture class. two paths:
- vendor the model code into our onboarding package (recommended for prod/private)
- allow trust_remote_code during conversion (fast, but needs review)

oliver: if you go trust_remote_code, you can run the tokenizer/model load like:
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("org/raptor-xl", trust_remote_code=True)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("org/raptor-xl", trust_remote_code=True)
```

zoe: another non-invasive trick: most failures come from the `architectures` entry in config.json. HF often has a new name (RaptorForCausalLM_v2). auto_map looks up known names. add a fallback name to config.json so our loader can map it to the generic class. e.g. patch config.json with:
```
"architectures": ["RaptorForCausalLM_v2", "RaptorForCausalLM"]
```
That lets our auto_map pick the older known name.

samir: tokenizer issue: quantization itself shouldn't mutate tokens, but our quant pipeline re-saves tokenizer artifacts and sometimes drops `special_tokens_map`. check the converted folder — do you have both `tokenizer.json` and `special_tokens_map.json`? run:
```
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('tmp/raptor'); print(t.special_tokens_map)"
```
If it's empty, add back the special token via `add_special_tokens` and re-save.

oliver: short-term workaround for eval: inject the missing token back into the tokenizer before running quantized inference:
```
tok.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens':['<|system|>']})
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tok))
model.save_pretrained('patched/raptor')
```

maya: will try the config.json patch + special token re-injection. curious if anyone has a minimal shim to vendor just the class so we don't enable trust_remote_code cluster-wide.

oliver: I wrote a tiny shim script for this last month — basically clones the repo, copies `raptor/model.py` into our onboarding `vendor/raptor` and rewrites imports. it's crude but safe. i'll drop it into the onboarding bucket.

zoe: note for longer term: add an onboarding checklist item — if repo uses nonstandard architectures or `trust_remote_code` we should either vendor the class or provide a reviewed stub. also add test that runs tokenization roundtrip after quantization.

maya: thanks. any quick eval tip to avoid re-running full bench? i can do a small stratified subset.

samir: run 200 prompts across the failure modes (system-msg + multi-turn) and diff tokenization. that'll catch missing special tokens quickly.

noah-bot: CI: conversion job #4567 requeued by oliver — tests will run in ~15m :robot_face: 

liam: thumbs up — ping here if you hit anything else. :thumbsup:
